title: Python for Excel & Office Work
summary: Made for Sheetah’s Excel learners. Let Python do the spreadsheet chores: read and write workbooks, filter, sort and total with pandas, clean messy sheets, build pivot-style summaries and format finished reports, ending with a one-click monthly report from a dozen messy sheets.
prereq: PY1 · Python Foundations at Beginner (variables, if, loops, lists). Knowing Excel helps but isn’t required.
outcomes: Open, read and write Excel workbooks from Python with openpyxl.
Read sheets into pandas DataFrames, then filter, sort, add columns and total them.
Write finished reports back to Excel, with several sheets and formatting.
Clean messy sheets: blanks, text numbers, dates and duplicates.
Build pivot-style summaries and lookups (groupby, pivot_table, merge).
Turn a month-end chore into a one-click report.

levels.name: Beginner
levels.who: Excel users taking their first steps in automating it.
levels.outcome: Read and write workbooks, filter, sort and total with pandas, and save tidy reports.

levels.name: Intermediate
levels.who: Most office learners, and what the Business Analyst and Data Storyteller certificates expect.
levels.outcome: Format reports from Python, combine many sheets, change exactly the rows you mean, and build the monthly report from messy files.

levels.name: Master
levels.who: People who will own their team’s reporting.
levels.outcome: Make the report robust to any mess, fast on big files, and run with one click.

project.title: A one-click monthly report built from a dozen messy sheets
project.brief: Twelve branch sheets in different states of mess become one clean, formatted report workbook. A checklist per level, hidden tests and three “explain your code” questions.
